Article Title: Google to everyone saying 'company threatened schools over using AI; says: We want to clarify, we are giving more …
Article Text:
Google to everyone saying 'company threatened schools over using AI; says: We want to clarify, we are giving more …

Here’s what Google said

We want to clarify what we announced today about our education services. Today’s announcements give schools more choice, not less. Here’s what we announced:

- Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be OFF 🔴 by default.

This is based on K-12 schools asking for more control over student use of AI services.

- Schools are in control: They can choose to turn ON 🟢 one, two, or all of these services individually.

- We are also updating Search for schools to make it better for learning. Specifically, AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork.

We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control.

That’s exactly why we are making these changes today to address the feedback we’ve heard from educators in recent months. And we’ll continue to engage deeply with educators to ensure we are giving schools more choice, more controls, and improved Search for learning.

Schools should have control over AI in classroom: Google

A report recently claimed that Google is turning off the AI tools – Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search for K-12 students starting next year. Google’s vice president of education, Chris Phillips, told The New York Times that the company’s AI features are “deeply integrated” into Search, meaning students cannot access one without the other. Soon after the announcement, many politicians and leaders including Bernie Sanders and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani voiced their outrage on social media. “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” Zohran Mamdani wrote on X (formerly Twitter). Bernie Sanders wrote that “Google is threatening schools,” referring to the policy as “extortion.”The company has now responded to the claims issuing the clarification on the change. “We want to clarify what we announced today about our education services. Today’s announcements give schools more choice, not less,” Google wrote on X.In the post, Google clarified that while Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search will be OFF by default, Schools will be in control. They can choose to turn ON one, two, or all of these services individually, the tech giant said.The company also published a blog post where it said that “schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach”.“After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search. Access to these products will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on,” it said.“We’ll share more specifics with schools in the coming months ahead of the changes rolling out so they have time to prepare and enable a smooth transition. Our goal is simple: provide school leaders the control and confidence to use AI products in classrooms as they see fit.We’ll continue to listen to feedback and evolve our approach as we work in partnership with schools, teachers, pedagogical experts, and parents on helping the next generation learn and thrive”.
Article Summary: A report recently claimed that Google is turning off the AI tools – Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search for K-12 students starting next year. “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” Zohran Mamdani wrote on X (formerly Twitter) Bernie Sanders wrote that ‘Google is threatening schools’ and referred to the policy as “extortion”

Article Title: Starting November 16, Apple is changing its App Store policy, to ban these apps on iPhones for users under 18
Article Text:
What Apple's announcement says

Apple is tightening its App Store rules to restrict minors’ access to dating apps and AI companions that offer sexual or romantic content, the company said in an announcement to developers. Under the updated policy, all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features must carry an 18+ age rating. Starting November 16, developers will be required to provide new content descriptors so their apps’ age ratings accurately reflect those features.The changes build on Apple’s broader child safety measures, including the global rollout of age assurance technology, expanded parental controls and additional protections for younger users. While most major dating services already limit access to adults, the policy could have broader implications for AI companion apps and services that include virtual relationships among their features.Platforms such as Character.AI and Replika allow users to create or interact with virtual companions, including friends, romantic partners and fantasy characters. Last year, xAI also introduced animated 3D companions with unlockable sexually explicit capabilities.As of last summer, leading AI companion apps had collectively recorded 220 million downloads worldwide across Apple’s App Store and Google Play.Apple is also introducing a content descriptor requiring developers to disclose whether their apps share a user’s real-world location with another person or group. Such features can raise privacy concerns, particularly when users are unaware their location is being shared.Starting November 16, 2026, App Store Connect will include new content descriptors to help ensure your app’s age ratings accurately reflect its features and are in accordance with local regulations.When completing the age rating questionnaire in App Store Connect, you’ll need to declare whether your app includes:Shared Location: Sharing of real-world location with another person or group.Dating and Relationships: Features that enable dating or relationship connections between real people and/or a virtual companion that engages a user in sexual or romantic content.You must provide these declarations when submitting an app update or making changes to your age rating questionnaire. All apps must have these declarations completed by January 12, 2027.Apps that include Dating and Relationships receive a minimum age rating of 18+. Apps that include Shared Location may not have an impact on their minimum age rating in some regions.In Brazil, local regulations require an A16 rating for Shared Location and an A18 rating for Dating and Relationships. If you believe your app qualifies for a lower age rating in Brazil — for example, if your app provides location sharing specifically designed for parents and children — you can request an official rating directly from Brazil’s Ministry of Justice and Public Security (MJSP/Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública). Once verified, the official rating will display on the App Store in Brazil.
Article Summary: Apple is tightening its App Store rules to restrict minors’ access to dating apps and AI companions. Under the updated policy, all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features must carry an 18+ age rating. Developers will be required to provide new content descriptors so their apps’ age ratings accurately reflect those features.

Article Title: After FBI arrested a Saudi National for hiding a spy device at OpenAI, employees said ‘not surprised’: Controls are so lenient that …
Article Text:
After FBI arrested a Saudi National for hiding a spy device at OpenAI, employees said ‘not surprised’: Controls are so lenient that …

OpenAI employees had raised security concerns for years

What did the Saudi national allegedly do

OpenAI has started strengthening its security systems

Former OpenAI employees say they were not surprised after the company discovered a hidden audio recording device in an executive conference room in October, as they had raised concerns about its internal security practices for years. According to a Reuters report, some employees warned OpenAI's leadership and board that its security controls were too weak and could allow outsiders, including foreign governments, to access sensitive information about its artificial intelligence (AI) technology. The concerns came into focus after FBI announced on October 13 that a Saudi national, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, had been arrested and charged with allegedly placing a hidden recording device in an OpenAI executive conference room. Alfozan was working as an engineer at the company at the time.According to five people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters, OpenAI employees raised concerns about the company's security practices even before ChatGPT launched in late 2022. Some employees believed that the company's internal controls were so weak that foreign governments or other outside actors could easily obtain sensitive details about its technology.They also said that employees with access to OpenAI's code could view details of projects that were not directly related to their work.Some staff members reportedly felt that OpenAI's leadership was more focused on keeping up with rivals such as Google and Anthropic than on strengthening security.According to a court filing cited by Reuters, Abdulrahman Alfozan allegedly used an AI tool designed for OpenAI employees to search for internal documents about executives travelling to Saudi Arabia. He also reportedly looked for information about which OpenAI officials were likely to attend meetings with Saudi ministers.The filing also stated that Alfozan was in regular contact with a Saudi royal who had tried to recruit him for a new AI venture in Saudi Arabia.OpenAI has reportedly begun taking steps to address its internal security concerns. Thibault Sottiaux, a senior executive overseeing product development, has recently taken charge of an internal effort to secure the company's systems. In August, Sottiaux reassigned around a quarter of OpenAI's production engineers to work on improving its security infrastructure, according to one person familiar with the matter.The company has also restricted access to sensitive work and said that its most sensitive projects are stored in separate code repositories with strict access controls. OpenAI said its main code repository does not contain all of its code or critical details of its AI models, including model weights, which determine how a model behaves. The company also said it now conducts regular security reviews of its internal tools.
Article Summary: OpenAI employees had raised security concerns for years. Some staff members felt that OpenAI's leadership was more focused on keeping up with rivals such as Google and Anthropic than on strengthening security. FBI announced on October 13 that a Saudi national, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, had been arrested and charged with allegedly placing a hidden recording device in an OpenAI conference room.

Article Title: Engineering graduate loses two fingers in 2025 accident, pays Rs 20,000 for customised artificial finger prosthesis; company misses 45-day deadline and delivers wrong-sized prosthesis without thumb im
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

A prosthesis that did not fit

Company fails to respond to complaint





CHENNAI: A customised artificial finger prosthesis was supposed to help a man regain some functionality after he lost two fingers in an accident. Instead, the Rs 20,000 product he received was allegedly of the wrong size and colour and did not have the promised thumb impression.The man approached the Pudukkottai district consumer commission after the company allegedly failed to correct the defects or refund his money. The commission has now ordered the company to return the amount and pay another Rs 20,000 towards compensation and litigation costs.In its order, commission president T Sekar and member S Sugunadevi held the company responsible for deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.“The opposite party assured a specific size, colour, and thumb impression, delivered a product that did not match, and then declined redress. This amounts to an unfair trade practice,” the order read.The complainant, an engineering graduate, had lost two fingers of his right hand in an accident. Seeking a customised replacement, he approached the company on June 23, 2025, and paid Rs 20,000 for an artificial finger prosthesis.The company allegedly promised to deliver the product within 45 days, with the required size and colour and a thumb impression.However, the promised deadline passed without delivery, the complainant said. He also alleged that the company did not respond to his phone calls.He eventually travelled to Chennai on September 5, 2025, to collect the prosthesis. But the product he received did not meet the specifications he had requested. It was of the wrong size and colour and lacked the promised thumb impression, according to his complaint.The man told the company that the prosthesis could not be used and sought a correction or replacement. He alleged that the company neither provided a replacement nor returned the money.The complainant further submitted that the delay and failure to supply a functional prosthesis affected his ability to appear for examinations.After the company did not respond to a legal notice seeking a refund and compensation, the man approached the consumer commission.Despite being served notice, the company neither appeared before the commission nor filed a response. The commission, therefore, proceeded to decide the case on the basis of the complainant's evidence and documents.It found that the prosthesis did not conform to the specifications promised by the company and was unusable for its intended purpose.“It was unusable for the purpose of which it was ordered, so the customized service was not performed as promised,” the commission noted.The commission also took note of the company's failure to rectify the defects, replace the product or refund the payment.Holding the company liable for deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, the commission observed that its conduct had caused the complainant hardship and mental agony.It directed the company to refund the Rs 20,000 paid for the prosthesis, along with Rs 10,000 as compensation for deficiency in service and mental agony and another Rs 10,000 towards the costs of the proceedings.
Article Summary: A man lost two fingers of his right hand in an accident. Seeking a customised replacement, he approached the company on June 23, 2025. He paid Rs 20,000 for an artificial finger prosthesis. The company allegedly promised to deliver the product within 45 days, with the required size and colour and a thumb impression.

Article Title: Old traditions get a new twist this Diwali
Article Text:
(AI Image) For generations, bursting crackershas been an integral part of Diwalicelebrations.

Popular fireworks get creative

The modern makeover

Drone crackers: Designed to appear like a drone.

Helicopter crackers: Crackers that spin or rise into the air, resembling a helicopter.

Remote-control crackers: Inspired products that combine movement with fireworks.

Coconut crackers: Designed in the shape of a coconut.

Lollipop sparklers: Colourful sparklers designed to resemble lollipops.

Traditional favourites

Kambi mathappu

Flower pots

Saravedi

Gilli crackers

Lakshmi bombs

Rockets

Did you know? Firecrackers originated in China, where bamboo stalks were thrown into fires to produce loud bursts to ward off evil. Sivakasi’s industry dates back to 1940.

Sweets get healthy

Sweet Description Mysore pak Karupatti Mysore pak made with palm jaggery instead of refined sugar Kaju katli Dark chocolate kaju katli and chocolate hazelnut kaju katli Peda Coffee hazelnut peda Gulab jamun Gulab jamun and rabdi ice cream

The modern decor picks

From hand-drawn kolams to ready-made

Solar mandala projector: A solar-powered, waterproof projector that cycles through seven colours and casts a mandala pattern on walls and floors.

Kolam rangoli: Interlocking loop designs resembling traditional chikku or knot kolams made of cream-coloured MDF/HDF board can be placed on the floor.

Detachable rangoli floor decorations: A ready-made arrangement with bead and mirror work, offering a reusable alternative to drawing a rangoli from scratch.

Did you know? A 13th-century inscription from Nellai refers to women being assigned the task of cleaning and decorating temple floors with kolams. It appears in 16th-century Tamil literature.

Regional treats in a new-age gift box

The modern makeover

Regional specialties: Sweets such as Tirunelveli halwa and Srivilliputhur palkova are being packed into curated gift boxes.

GI-tagged treats: Geographical indication-tagged sweets and savouries are being positioned as gifts that celebrate the food heritage of their regions.

Fusion hampers: Chocolate-covered traditional sweets, chocolate-and-mithai combinations and contemporary dessert boxes.

Health-conscious gifting: Sugar-free sweets and hampers featuring millets.

Six yards of tradition, a whole new style

The vintage revival

Checks (kattam): Classic patterns returning in contrasting colours and combinations.

Stripes (vari): Traditional stripes reinterpreted in bold colour combinations.

Peacock, parrot and elephant buttas: Bird and animal motifs inspired by temple art.

Rudraksham and temple borders: Traditional motifs and gopuram-inspired designs.

Paisley and floral buttas: Vintage patterns making a comeback in festive collections.

The price tag

Category Price Semi-silk sarees Rs 1,555 onwards Pure Kanchipuram silk Rs 3,135 onwards Premium festive silk Rs 18,000–58,950

Did you know? Kanchivaram silk weaving is believed to have a history of more than 1,500 years, with its origins traced to the Pallava period. The craft evolved under dynasties, including the Cholas and Vijayanagara rulers.





An oil bath, idlis, chicken curry, and pattimandram (a debating style in which participants argue in a humorous manner) — Diwali is usual in Tamil households, except some traditions are getting new-age upgrades, with varieties such as karupatti mysore pak, dark chocolate kaju katli and coffee hazelnut peda.A Coimbatore-based brand, Petti-kadai, offers “The Geo Tagged Sweet Box”, a 500 collection: Tirunelveli halwa, Srivilliputhur palkova, Palapatti ghee Mysore pak, Kovilpatti kadalai mittai and Kumbakonam dry jamun.“Detachable” kolam designs are also finding their way into homes decor as a convenient alternative.M D Muthukumaraswamy, director of National Folklore Support Centre, an NGO, said Diwali has moved away from being just about fireworks. “Increased awareness and government intervention has limited the use of loud crackers. People now focus more on their attire and food,” he said.Even shopping at Ranganathan Street has made way for home delivery, he said. Lighting lamps, he said, has not traditionally been a major part of celebrations down south. But homes are increasingly being decorated with lamps much like during Karthigai Deepam.“Festivals give adults a break and children a reason to celebrate.Diwali falls in Aippasi, during heavy rain. Without these celebrations, it would be just another day,” he said.For generations, bursting crackers has been an integral part of Diwali celebrations. Cracker manufacturers are experimenting with shapes, designs and interactive features to make fireworks more appealing, particularly to children and younger buyers. Some newer products borrow their designs from everyday objects, toys and popular gadgets.Traditional sweets are returning with newer ingredients, flavours and combinations. While some sweet makers are replacing refined sugar with natural alternatives, others are experimenting with chocolate, coffee and exotic flavours.Drawing a kolam at the entrance of the house is a familiar ritual in Tamil households. Traditionally made with rice flour or coloured powder, these decorations are now finding alternatives to traditional floor decorations.Diwali gifting has traditionally revolved around boxes of sweets and savouries shared with family, friends, neighbours and colleagues. Tirunelveli halwa and Srivilliputhur palkova are regional halwas that have long been part of the festive exchange. Gifting is moving beyond the quantity of sweets in a box to the story behind them. Regional identity, premium packaging, ingredient choices and the experience of discovering different specialties are becoming part of the appeal.Kanchi silk, ‘podikattam’ (checkered) saris and ‘pavadai-sattai’ have long been part of TN's festive wardrobe. Designers are revisiting vintage colours, prints and patterns, combining traditional weaving techniques with natural dyes and contemporary embroidery. Traditional silk aesthetic is also moving beyond saris. These designs are being adapted for shirts and kurtis. Reversible designs and lightweight silk blends offer more options for buyers who want traditional elements in contemporary silhouettes.Traditional patterns, once associated with heirloom saris, are finding their way into contemporary festive collections.
Article Summary: Firecrackers originated in China, where bamboo stalks were thrown into fires to produce loud bursts to ward off evil. Kanchivaram silk weaving is believed to have a history of more than 1,500 years. Sweets such as Tirunelveli halwa and Srivilliputhur palkova are being packed into curated gift boxes.

Article Title: WhatsApp may soon roll out new Shortcuts for Android and iPhone users: Here's how they are likely to work
Article Text:
How the new Message Text Actions feature of WhatsApp is said to work

Works with sent and received messages

What each shortcut does

Privacy remains unchanged

Availability

WhatsApp is reportedly rolling out a new feature which could make it easier for users to interact with the information shared in WhatsApp Chats, as reported by WABetaInfo. Available only to some select users, the feature called "Message Text Actions" or "Smart Text Actions," is designed to automatically detect details like phone numbers, dates, addresses and email IDs, then offers contextual shortcuts directly within conversations. As per the report, the feature is being introduced on both Android and iOS users of WhatsApp and is made to reduce the need to copy and paste information from other apps.The feature is created to automatically identify supported text formats within both incoming and outgoing messages. Whenever WhatsApp spots a phone number, date, address or email address in a message, it will automatically draw a dotted underline beneath that text. When the user taps on the underline a popup will appear on the screen that shows the text WhatsApp detected at the top. This will enable the users to check the text and make sure that the app picked the correct message. Users who don’t wish to use the shortcut can simply ignore it and can carry on with their conversation.One of the important aspects of this update is that the shortcuts are not limited to messages received from contacts.The feature also works for the messages sent by the user, as this will make it easier for the users to interact with the information which was already present in the previous conversation. The report further adds that WhatsApp will also display the detected text in a pop-up menu, enabling the users to verify that the app has identified the information correctly before they proceed with any action.* Phone numbers: Users can copy the number, add it to contacts or place a call through their phone carrier. For business numbers, they can also see the business’s information.* Dates and times: Users are able to add the date to their calendar, copy it or make a new event within WhatsApp.* Addresses: Users are also allowed to copy the address and open it directly in maps.* Email addresses: Users can also open the address in their mail app or copy it.WABetaInfo noted that some of these actions already existed, but WhatsApp is now making them easier to find and use.After a user picks an action, WhatsApp asks whether it was useful. If the user says it wasn’t, they can say whether the app detected the wrong text or the action wasn’t needed. WABetaInfo said this only sends WhatsApp a flag and not the message content. The tracker also said the detection happens entirely on the device, using pattern-matching rules, so WhatsApp never receives the message content or the suggestion. As a result, the feature does not affect end-to-end encryption.The feature is currently being rolled out to select users running the latest versions of WhatsApp on Android and iOS, with wider availability expected in the coming weeks.
Article Summary: WhatsApp is reportedly rolling out a new feature which could make it easier for users to interact with the information shared in WhatsApp Chats. The feature called "Message Text Actions" or "Smart Text Actions," is designed to automatically detect details like phone numbers, dates, addresses and email IDs. As per the report, the feature is being introduced on both Android and iOS users of WhatsApp.

Article Title: In 1990, Oregon trucked 580,000 tyres up to 200 miles to shore up slide-prone US 42; net cost $10 a ton, and federal engineers called it the largest tyre fill for a landslide correction project
Article Text:
AI Representation: Oregon used 580,000 discarded tyres to stabilise a landslide-prone US Route. Image credits: Chatgpt

Highway construction reactivated an existing landslide

Four suppliers delivered 580,000 shredded tyres

Oregon recycling program reduced the material cost to $10 per

Shredded tyre materials. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

FHWA identified it as the largest known landslide-correction project

Discarded car tyres usually create a waste management problem, but Oregon engineers found an unusual use for thousands of them during a highway repair project in 1990. A slope along a road embankment was unstable and adding more regular soil would have put more weight on ground that was already moving. Instead, the Oregon Department of Transportation (ODOT) replaced part of the heavy soil embankment with shredded scrap tyres, a lighter material that cut the load on the unstable slope. The work took place in 1990 on US 42, the Coos Bay-Roseburg Highway, about 25 miles west of Roseburg in southwestern Oregon. ODOT’s report lists the route as Oregon state route 35. The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) later cited it as the largest known use of shredded tyres in a landslide correction project.The project was carried out in 1990 on US Highway 42, also known as ODOT Highway 35 along the Coos Bay-Roseburg route about 25 miles west of Roseburg in southwestern Oregon, which is referred to as Oregon State Road 35 in the ODOT engineering report. Modification of the embankment through Highway upgrading led to the reactivation of an old landslide underneath the road due to the increased load.The need for a repair measure that could stabilise the slope without increasing its load required a design whereby part of the soil embankment was replaced by shredded chips. The soil from excavation was used to create a counterweight at the bottom of the slope. ODOT documented the work in its February 1991 report, Experimental Project: Use of Shredded Tires for Lightweight Fill. The job needed about 5,800 tons of shredded tyres, roughly 580,000 tyres. Four suppliers trucked them to the site from 150 to 275 miles away, according to the 1993 paper by Richard J. Upton and George Machan in Transportation Research Record 1422. The chips arrived in 100-cubic-yard trucks, each carrying 28 tons. Workers placed them in three-foot lifts and compacted each lift with a D-8 dozer. Handling the material caused some trouble. Exposed steel wire in the shreds punctured some of the dump-truck tyres used on the job. The 1993 paper by Upton and Machan covers the supply and construction in more detail.Oregon’s Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ) backed the project through a program that reimbursed the productive use of scrap tyres. The shredded material cost $30 per ton and DEQ refunded $20, bringing the material cost down to $10 per ton. Placing and compacting it added $8.33 per ton, for an installed cost of $18.33 per ton. The reimbursement made shredded tyres a practical option for the repair.After construction, the tyre fill got a three-foot compacted soil cap on the top and side slopes. The road surface went on top: 23 inches of aggregate base under 8 inches of asphalt pavement. The thickest part of the tyre embankment was about 12.5 feet. Under the weight of the cover, it settled about 20 inches, roughly 13 percent of its original thickness.ODOT monitored the structure with slope inclinometers, piezometers, settlement plates and survey hubs. The 1993 study found that the pavement’s initial deflection was about double the deflection over an earth embankment.The project appeared in the FHWA’s User Guidelines for Waste and Byproduct Materials in Pavement Construction. The guidelines called Oregon’s use of about 580,000 scrap tyres the largest known use of shredded tyres in a landslide correction project. That record covers landslide repairs only, not every highway embankment that used recycled tyres. The FHWA also set up another project in Colorado where about 400,000 to 450,000 tyres were used in an interstate Highway embankment. The repair conducted in Oregon showed that old tyres could be used as a lightweight material for construction purposes, especially when normal soil puts pressure on the unstable land.
Article Summary: Oregon used 580,000 discarded tyres to stabilise a landslide-prone US Route. The Federal Highway Administration said it was the largest known use of shredded tyres in a landslide correction project. The shredded material cost $30 per ton and DEQ refunded $20, bringing the material cost down to $10 per ton.

Article Title: Edouard Mendy becomes patron of Senegal school that inspired a project providing free education, digital learning and clean water to local communities
Article Text:
PC: Yakar Project

Yakar Project began with a 2015 visit to ADE School

How did Mendy become associated with ADE School

Tablets and computers support learning at Yakar School

Clean water, football and local initiatives form Yakar Project's wider work

In May 2025, Edouard Mendy was named patron of ADE School, a new role supporting education in Senegal. A 2015 visit to ADE School helped inspire the Yakar Project. Established in 2020, the organisation works to improve access to education, clean water and community support.According to the Yakar Project, its education work also includes Yakar School in Keur Massar, where children receive free education. In March 2025, the project launched a digital learning hub at the school using the PowerZ educational platform. The initiative gave students access to tablets and computers, allowing them to explore subjects such as mathematics and history through digital learning.The Yakar Project began with a 2015 visit to ADE School. The school is in Thiaroye, an underprivileged suburb on the outskirts of Dakar. The visit showed how education, football and community support could help improve children's lives. Five years later, the project was established to turn this idea into action.Its name comes from the Wolof word ‘Yakar’, which means hope. The organisation aims to build a self-sustaining network of local people who can bring positive changes to their communities. Its work focuses on quality education, access to clean water, and community empowerment.It also aims to address immediate needs while helping people become more independent.In May 2025, Mendy was officially named patron of ADE School. Located in Thiaroye, the school became an important part of the story behind the Yakar Project. The organisation says the appointment deepens his commitment to Thiaroye.His involvement also reflects the project's wider focus on education and opportunities for children. The initiative grew from the belief that education and community support can help young people build better futures.The Yakar Project also supports education through Yakar School in Keur Massar. The school provides free education and access to digital learning facilities. In March 2025, the project launched a digital learning hub using the PowerZ educational platform. Students received access to tablets and computers as part of the initiative.The platform allows them to explore subjects such as mathematics and history through educational games and digital activities. It also helps them develop digital skills alongside their regular studies. The project sees technology as a way to support teachers and make learning more engaging for children.Education is one of four main areas of work undertaken by the Yakar Project. The others are clean water, sport for development, and ChangeKeepers. The organisation is working to build sustainable water wells that provide drinking water to schools and villages across Senegal. Its sports programme uses football to encourage inclusion and provides equipment and funding for community pitches.Through ChangeKeepers, it offers grants and training to Senegalese social entrepreneurs who are developing local initiatives. The project also reports having built three wells and distributed 500 football jerseys. Its supporters include Nike, PowerZ, Pro: Direct Soccer, Afrikicks and Revibe. These programmes form part of its wider effort to strengthen communities and create opportunities across Senegal.
Article Summary: Edouard Mendy was named patron of ADE School in May 2025. The school is in Thiaroye, an underprivileged suburb on the outskirts of Dakar. In March 2025, the project launched a digital learning hub at the school using the PowerZ educational platform.

Article Title: Mother fights to save Leicester leisure centre pool as council considers closure, warning her severely disabled son could lose his only accessible swimming facility
Article Text:
PC: Wikipedia

What makes pool facilities essential for Susan Wilder’s son

Family struggles to find an accessible swimming pool for disabled son

New Parks closure plan sparks concern over disabled son's swimming access

How does the council plan to support swimmers with complex disabilities

A mother in Leicester is urging the city council to keep New Parks Leisure Centre open, warning that its closure could leave her severely disabled son without access to a suitable swimming pool. Susan Wilder, 67, said the centre was the only facility she had found that could accommodate her 19-year-old son, who uses a wheelchair full-time and has complex physical, visual and hearing impairments.According to the BBC, swimming provides him with his only form of cardiovascular exercise and gives him a sense of freedom. Leicester City Council is consulting on proposals to close the leisure centre and invest £8 million in transforming Leicester Leys Leisure Centre.Wilder said her son had been swimming at New Parks Leisure Centre for 19 years. He attends once one week and twice the next. She explained that he cannot use a standard pool chair because of his complex disabilities and requires specialist facilities to enter the water safely.He requires a poolside changing room with a ceiling-track hoist and a changing bed. The bed is brought to the poolside before he is transferred into the water using the hoist.Wilder said, "He loves the freedom of it and it's also the only cardiovascular exercise he gets.”"He has no speech, but he just generally loves the water."Wilder said her family had searched for alternative swimming facilities, including centres outside Leicestershire, but had been unable to find a suitable option for her son.Wilder said, "We're willing to travel with him, we're willing to travel out of the county, but there's nowhere available to meet his needs.”She explained that while many disabled people could use swimming pools with the help of a pool chair, her son's needs were different. He requires facilities that allow him to be transferred from his changing bed into the water using a ceiling-track hoist.She said, "You have to look at people's needs to be able to access a swimming pool in the correct way. It's not just for my son, it's for anybody that has the disabilities that he's got.”Leicester City Council has described New Parks as the city's least used leisure centre and plans to spend £8 million transforming Leicester Leys Leisure Centre under the proposals.A petition calling for New Parks to be saved has received more than 2,150 signatures. However, Wilder said Leicester Leys would be too busy for her son because of his multi-sensory impairment, which includes hearing and visual impairments. She said he would not be able to swim there even if a pool hoist were installed.Wilder also expressed concern that the future of New Parks might already have been decided.According to Leicester Mercury, she said, “It’s a dif­fer­ent feel­ing; it’s sens­ory and helps relax him. I just want to make the coun­cil under­stand how import­ant it is that he and oth­ers get access to be able to swim.”“This is why I’m so against New Parks clos­ing.”Leicester City Council said it had spoken to a range of swimming pool users during the consultation to understand their individual requirements and explore whether their needs could be met at other sites.A council spokesperson said, "All city council swimming pools offer disabled pool hoists designed to support users with diverse mobility requirements and transfer preferences, including compatibility with standard slings and adapted poolside chairs.”"After speaking with Sue, we understand that her son needs deeper water, so Aylestone Leisure Centre is making some small adaptions that will mean this centre will also be suitable for them and others to use.”"No decision has been made on the future of New Parks Leisure Centre, and we encourage everyone to have their say by November 3rd."
Article Summary: Leicester City Council is consulting on proposals to close New Parks Leisure Centre. Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

Is Aadhaar mandatory for a digital Life Certificate

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a criticalseverity warning. (Reuters photo)

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities

BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems.Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual.

Article Title: Apple’s latest beta puts AI to work in conversations, at the gym and in the Health app
Article Text:
Apple Watch Showing the Wrong Time After Daylight Saving? How to Fix It

How much of a conversation is worth keeping?

A better reason to glance at the Watch between sets

Someone gives you an address. You catch the street name but miss the building number, and the conversation has already moved on. On the Apple Watch Series 12, a double press of the Digital Crown brings up the last 15 seconds as text. Apple calls it Live Rewind. Fifteen seconds sounds stingy until you think about how little of a conversation you usually need back.Live Rewind and Siri Recap have begun developer beta testing with iOS 27.3, with a public beta to follow. Both are opt-in features for the Series 12 and Ultra 4. Live Rewind has the clearer pitch. A glance at the wrist might be enough to recover a name or a number. The snippet disappears automatically unless it’s saved to the Siri app, and there’s an option to ask Siri about something in it.The double press also triggers a chime, even in silent mode, and an animation on the Watch. That makes an otherwise subtle gesture visible to the people around the wearer. It also gives the feature an interesting social wrinkle. In some conversations, it may still feel more natural to ask someone to repeat themselves.Siri Recap turns a conversation into a title and a short list of key points. Users can choose when and where it runs, and unsaved recaps are deleted within seven days.Apple says the feature does not identify speakers or retain raw audio. That makes it easier to see the appeal as a memory aid, though the lack of speaker attribution matters when the most important detail in a meeting is who agreed to do what.The real test for both features in India will be what happens when a conversation slips from English into Hindi, two people speak at once and a name or deadline gets buried in the middle. Live Rewind only has to recover a few words to be useful. Siri Recap has a harder job. It has to know which few words mattered.Fitness+ Gym Strength addresses a familiar gym problem. It’s easy to track how long a workout took. Figuring out what to lift today, and whether to go heavier than last week, takes more thought. Apple builds a four-week programme around the user’s goals, experience, schedule and available equipment, then adjusts it based on how training goes.The iPhone or iPad holds the plan and the exercise videos. On the Watch, users can check the next exercise, see the suggested reps and weight, and log what they actually managed. That division suits the gym. A video is worth pulling out the phone for when an exercise is unfamiliar. Checking whether the next set calls for eight reps or 12 should take a glance. The more revealing test will come when a three-session week turns into a one-session week and the plan has to adapt.The redesigned Health app, back in beta, offers a different sort of first impression. Health Age will probably get the first tap. It’s hard to resist finding out how old your phone thinks you are. The movement assessments have more potential to bring people back, especially if they can explain what’s changed over time in terms that help people decide how much to move or train.Gym Strength makes the strongest case for keeping the phone in the bag. Live Rewind is the more distinctive addition. After years of the Apple Watch tapping its wearer to deliver a notification, there’s finally an interesting reason to tap it back.
Article Summary: Live Rewind and Siri Recap have begun developer beta testing with iOS 27.3, with a public beta to follow. Both are opt-in features for the Series 12 and Ultra 4. Live Rewind only has to recover a few words to be useful. Siri Recap has to know which few words mattered.

Article Title: Chip smuggler details how a single loophole is letting banned South Korean RAM slip into China’s AI labs
Article Text:
High Bandwidth Memory

How high-cost, banned memory is ‘shipped’ into China

Prices skyrocket as AI race accelerates

Advanced memory chips barred under strict export controls are slipping across borders directly into Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) laboratories, guided by a regulatory blind spot in international trade rules, a report has said. A memory smuggler has reportedly revealed how export-controlled High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) manufactured in South Korea by Samsung and SK Hynix reaches mainland China. Under current US and South Korean trade restrictions, standalone exports of cutting-edge HBM units to China are outright prohibited. Yet the smuggler, who runs a chip design venture, identified an easy detour around the embargo, The Information reports.The report (via Tom’s Hardware) details that regulatory export controls measure only the raw computing performance of the server processor itself, without evaluating secondary components attached to the board. By designing cheap, low-performing processors that sit comfortably beneath the legal restriction limits, the firm attaches premium Samsung and SK Hynix HBM directly onto the modules. As the central processor is deemed harmless under export criteria, the full board clears customs inspections without raising red flags.Transporting the hardware into mainland China involves a delicate process. Firstly, the low-end boards with top-tier memory first arrive in Hong Kong. From there, daily commuters carry the hardware inside personal luggage across the border into Shenzhen. Once inside Shenzhen, the hardware is taken to local workshops. Technicians heat the circuit boards to soften the solder, carefully pry off the valuable HBM units and throw away the cheap processors and host boards.Even though melting and lifting memory off boards carries a high failure rate, the surging street value of functional HBM units makes the risky operation profitable.The black market for advanced memory has expanded rapidly alongside China’s push to train competitive AI models. A Shenzhen-based broker facilitating transactions between smugglers and hardware-starved domestic tech firms noted that street prices have reached historic highs.“A year ago, a single HBM3E unit changed hands in China for several hundred dollars. Today it’s about $4,000,” the broker told The Information.Modern AI accelerators require between six and eight high-end memory units to operate. At current black-market rates, brokers generate $24,000 to $32,000 for the memory bundle needed to run a single AI graphics processing unit (GPU).
Article Summary: A memory smuggler has reportedly revealed how export-controlled High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) reaches mainland China. Under current US and South Korean trade restrictions, standalone exports of cutting-edge HBM units to China are outright prohibited. The smuggler, who runs a chip design venture, identified an easy detour around the embargo.

Article Title: From bumper discounts to ‘free gifts’: How to spot festive online shopping scams
Article Text:
Bumper discounts that don’t add up

“Free gift” links and fake contests

Fake shopping sites and apps

Fake delivery and customer-care messages

Safer shopping habits

What to do if you’ve been scammed

The festive season is the busiest time of the year for online shopping, and also for online fraud. As sale banners go up and deal alerts flood phones, scammers move in with their own versions: websites that copy famous brands, discounts that seem too generous to pass up, and “free gift” links that arrive on WhatsApp just when people are hunting for bargains. The pressure and excitement to lock a deal before it disappears often makes it easy to click first and think later. Also, many of such traps look convincing as they come with real logos, polished pages and some urgent countdowns which compel you to click. Knowing the warning signs can save you from losing money, card details or access to your accounts. Here is how to tell a genuine festive offer from a fake one.A latest-model smartphone at half price, or a branded watch for a few hundred rupees, should make you stop and think. Genuine sales do cut prices, but fraudsters set theirs absurdly low because they never plan to deliver. Compare the price with the same product on the brand’s official store or a trusted marketplace. If it is far lower than everywhere else, treat it as a warning. Countdown timers and “only three left” banners are also pressure tactics, and they are easy for anyone to fake.We often receive messages announcing that we have won some festive hamper, or a voucher or even a gold coin in some lucky draw.But what is important here is that we never participated in any such draw and its always turn out to be a scam. The link which is shared in the message may direct you to a form which asks for your address, credit card details and may also charge small ‘shipping fee’. But it’s important that you never pay to receive a prize. Also, keep in mind that you never need a UPI PIN or an OTP to receive money or a gift, because those are used only to send payments or confirm them. If a page asks for either, close it.Scammers always try to lure the customers by creating copycat websites with addresses that are slightly off. For instance, they may include some extra words, a swapped letter or an unusual ending. So, before to make any purchase just thoroughly check the web address and look for contact details and a clear return policy. Also, be cautious about the pages that accept only payment made by UPI transfer or bank transfer. Avoid downloading ant app from the links shared in chats or text messages. It’s important that you always download and install the apps only from the official Play Store or App Store, as the fake files present in forwarded messages can steal your data and also read all your messages.During the time of festive sale, many of use receive text messages saying that your parcel is stuck and you will have to pay a small amount or update your address details by clicking on the given link. Scammers also post fake customer-care numbers on social media and search results, then ask you to share an OTP or install a screen-sharing app in order to fix the order. It’s important to note that the real companies never ask for any of these details. You can always check your order status inside the shopping app and can find the customer care number by visiting the official website of the company.* It is advisable to type the complete website address by yourself or always access the service via its official app and avoid clicking on any random link present in a message.* Always use the platform’s official checkout system. Cards or cash on delivery can offer more protection than a direct transfer to an individual.* Always keep a check on the reviews of the service. Some of the glowing reviews can be fake, so read a mix and check when they were posted online.* It’s always important to stay alert. So, enable two-step verification, and use a different password for each shopping account.* In case an offer makes you feel rushed, check it with the brand before paying.Act fast. Call your bank immediately to block your card or account, and change the passwords on any accounts you may have exposed. Uninstall any app you were told to download. In India, report the fraud on the national cybercrime helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in, as early reporting improves the chances of freezing the money. Report and block the sender, and warn friends and family.A good rule for the season is simple: if the deal seems too good to be true, or you can’t verify it, walk away.
Article Summary: The festive season is the busiest time of the year for online shopping. As sale banners go up and deal alerts flood phones, scammers move in with their own versions. Knowing the warning signs can save you from losing money, card details or access to your accounts.

Article Title: Anthropic adds new rule to Claude Code for game clones; company says: Using Claude to infringe IP is against our...
Article Text:
Anthropic’s Claude Code and Opus 5.5 now block video game cloning

AI game clones had already become a headache for developers

Claude is now left to judge what counts as a clone

Anthropic has added a new rule to Claude Code that stops the AI coding tool from recreating existing video games, even if a user renames the copy or calls it original. The two-sentence instruction tells Claude to build original games, games in a genre and games from a user’s own designs and assets, but not a recreation of a specific title.Anthropic engineer Addy Osmani confirmed the change on October 30. He said the sentences were added to Claude Code’s prompt on Opus 5.5 because using Claude to infringe IP is against the company’s usage policy. Original games should keep working, he added, and anyone wrongly refused can send the case to him.The rule was first spotted by an X user called chasm, who traced it to a flag named “tengu_heron_brook” that reached Claude Code around October 27. There is reportedly no setting to switch it off. The text also sits inside Claude Code version 2.1.314, while separate Opus 5.5 settings suggest the model can receive the guidance on its own.The timing is not random. Steam Next Fest last month was flooded with low-effort games, and itch.io has reportedly seen the number of new game pages double in two months. Some studios chose to hide their work. Alliance Arts and Who You pulled the Drunken Goddess Reflux demo despite 25,000 wishlists, while Digital Sun moved ReVamp to a private Discord playtest.The reverse engineering community has felt it too. Game decompilation hub decomp.dev shut down last month, with its maintainer saying fast AI tools had turned a patient community effort into a numbers race.That is where the trouble starts. Independent tests found that Opus 5.5 still agreed to help with a decompilation and a static recompilation of Pokemon Diamond, treating both as different from rebuilding the game. Developers report otherwise elsewhere. One filed a GitHub issue after Claude refused to help build board-wargame modules for paying customers, made from games those customers own.Reverse engineering tasks are also being refused. A developer testing his own software found that switching to Opus 4.8 let his work continue, and a Reddit user said their account was suspended over Opus 5.5 and a reverse engineering tool, then reinstated.The rule also leaves open questions. A straight copy of Tetris would be blocked, but a game in the Tetris genre should pass. Where a mashup, such as Mario dropped into Elden Ring, falls is anyone’s guess. Claude is left to judge that on its own, with only two sentences to go on.Workarounds are easy, too. Anyone set on cloning a game can move to rival coding tools or open-weight models that have no such rule. Anthropic has also not said whether the rule will extend to its other models.For now, the rule blocks the easiest request, a named game rebuilt from scratch. It does little to stop a determined copier, and it has already caught some developers working on their own projects.
Article Summary: Claude is now left to judge what counts as a clone. Anthropic has not said whether the rule will extend to its other models. It does little to stop a determined copier and it has already caught some developers working on their own projects.

Article Title: Anthropic and OpenAI ban employees from wearing company badges outside office; give 'guidelines' on friendship, romance as they become targets of ...

OpenAI warns staff about approaches outside work

“Everyone wants to find out about developments and information at the cutting edge of technology. They want firsthand information. They want to talk to these employees, but the employees generally avoid discussing anything,”

Protests and attacks add to security concerns

Employees’ families describe concerns about trust

“I also pay attention to safety and remind my child to be careful, because he can easily become a target. They try not to talk about their work at all. They keep it more about sports, hobbies, hiking and food,”

Anthropic and OpenAI are reportedly telling employees to conceal company badges and logos in public. According to the New York Post, OpenAI has instructed staff not to wear items carrying its logo outside the office, while Anthropic reminds workers to hide their badges and has largely restricted branded merchandise. The precautions come amid concerns about espionage, unwanted approaches and hostility towards people working in artificial intelligence (AI).OpenAI’s security training warns that spies may offer money, friendship or romance to obtain confidential information. The guidance reportedly concerns attempts to exploit personal relationships, not a ban on employees forming them. Anthropic has also reported people trying to photograph its offices, adding to concerns about how easily workers can be identified.OpenAI’s security sessions describe methods ranging from overhearing conversations in cafes to bribery and attempts to build personal relationships. In one incident reported by The Wall Street Journal, a stranger approached an OpenAI employee at a San Francisco playground and gradually steered the conversation towards work. The publication claimed that the person was a spy. Employees are also reminded to use privacy screens on public transport and erase meeting-room whiteboards before leaving.Miao Hong, managing partner of Silicon Valley Future Capital and an investor in both companies, said that people repeatedly approach AI workers seeking inside information.he said.The precautions also come against a backdrop of hostility towards AI companies and their employees. In March, activists wrote messages outside OpenAI’s San Francisco offices urging staff to quit over its Pentagon agreement. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s home was targeted in two separate incidents in April 2026, according to the report.One suspect allegedly threw a Molotov cocktail at the property and subsequently threatened OpenAI’s headquarters. Two other suspects were accused of firing a shot outside his home two days later. All three were arrested and charged, pleaded not guilty and are awaiting trial.Meanwhile, Anthropic disclosed in its stock-market listing filing that it spent $2.7 million on personal security services for CEO Dario Amodei, the report added.The father of an Anthropic employee, who asked not to be named, said that his son and colleagues avoid discussing work socially.he said.He also described the difficulty of judging whether new acquaintances were interested in his son personally or in his employer.he said.

Article Title: Zomato launches Host Mode, lets users hide menu prices from guests: Here’s how it works
Article Text:
Designed to make hosting more comfortable

How Host Mode works

Feature inspired by customer feedback

Food delivery platform Zomato has launched a new feature called Host Mode, aimed at making group food ordering more comfortable by hiding menu prices from guests while allowing hosts to retain control over the final bill. The new feature, which is now available to users across India, enables guests to browse restaurant menus and add dishes to the cart without seeing the cost of individual items. Hosts can later review the complete bill and place the order after authenticating with a passcode, fingerprint, or face lock.According to Zomato, the feature addresses a common social situation where guests often hesitate to order their preferred dishes when someone else is paying. The company said many diners tend to choose less expensive items or leave the decision to the host, while hosts typically want their guests to order freely without worrying about the cost.With Host Mode enabled, prices are removed from restaurant menus and the cart, allowing guests to focus solely on choosing what they would like to eat. The total bill remains hidden until the host decides to exit the mode and review the order.The company said the feature is particularly relevant during the festive season, when families and friends frequently gather and order food together.Users can activate the feature by tapping the Host Mode option available on the app's home screen, restaurant menu pages, or through the preferences section in their profile.Once enabled, prices disappear across menus and the cart, and guests can add items without seeing any pricing information. When the order is ready, the host can tap the option to exit Host Mode, authenticate using biometric verification or device security credentials, and view the complete bill, including any discounts or savings, before placing the order.Zomato said only the host can reveal the bill, ensuring that pricing details remain private throughout the ordering process.The company revealed that Host Mode originated from a suggestion shared by a Zomato customer on social media. According to Zomato, the idea was developed and rolled out on the app within 72 hours, with the goal of making social hosting and food ordering more seamless for customers. The launch adds to Zomato's ongoing efforts to introduce features aimed at improving user experience on its food delivery platform, particularly around social and group ordering occasions.
Article Summary: Zomato has launched a new feature called Host Mode, aimed at making group food ordering more comfortable by hiding menu prices. The new feature, which is now available to users across India, enables guests to browse restaurant menus and add dishes to the cart without seeing the cost of individual items.

How can users access it on Google Pay

How do virtual try-on and image search work

Article Title: Hackers hit Nvidia’s cloud development platform: What the company said in notification sent to affected customers
Article Text:
Nvidia

What Nvidia told affected users: Read notification

We are writing to inform you that NVIDIA Corporation ("NVIDIA") has experienced a security incident that may affect the security of your data. NVIDIA is providing this notice to you with details of the incident, our response, and resources available to you to help protect your personal information from possible misuse.

What Happened?

Our incident investigation identified unauthorized activity affecting the NVIDIA Brev platform from October 4 through October 20, 2026. Nvidia has been hit by another cyberattack, this time targeting its Brev cloud development platform. Citing the customer notice, Tom’s Hardware reported that Nvidia launched an internal investigation after spotting unidentified activity on the platform. The probe determined that malicious actors may have accessed data stored on Brev systems, specifically compromising Secure Shell (SSH) keys configured by the service.In its communication to users, Nvidia confirmed the security breach and outlined the immediate technical steps taken to protect developer systems, while also stating that it replaced the compromised SSH keys with new credentials. The company added that its team has found no evidence showing the exposed keys were improperly used.The breach at Nvidia arrives amid a broader series of security incidents aimed at AI infrastructure providers and developer cloud platforms. For example, on October 30, cybersecurity firm Wiz published a report detailing what it described as a “Black October” for AI developer services.
